{{short description|The polynomial hierarchy is contained in  probabilistic Turing machine in polynomial time}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2026}}
'''Toda's theorem''' is a result in [[computational complexity theory]] that was proven by [[Seinosuke Toda]] in his paper "PP is as Hard as the Polynomial-Time Hierarchy"<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Toda|first=Seinosuke|date=October 1991|title=PP is as Hard as the Polynomial-Time Hierarchy|url=http://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/0220053|journal=[[SIAM Journal on Computing]]|volume=20|issue=5|pages=865–877|doi=10.1137/0220053|issn=0097-5397|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and was given the 1998 [[Gödel Prize]].

==Statement==
The theorem states that the entire [[PH (complexity)|polynomial hierarchy PH]] is contained in P<sup>PP</sup>; this implies a closely related statement, that PH is contained in P<sup>#P</sup>.

==Definitions==
[[Sharp-P|#P]] is the class of problems of the form of exactly counting the number of solutions to a polynomially-verifiable question (that is, to a question in [[NP (complexity)|NP]]), while loosely speaking, [[PP (complexity)|PP]] is the class of problems for which there is a [[polynomial-time algorithm]] that gives a correct answer more than half the time. The class P<sup>#P</sup> consists of all problems that can be solved in polynomial time if you have access to instantaneous answers to any counting problem in #P (polynomial time relative to a #P [[Baker-Gill-Solovay theorem|oracle]]). Thus Toda's theorem implies that for any problem in the polynomial hierarchy there is a deterministic [[polynomial-time Turing reduction]] to a [[Counting problem (complexity)|counting problem]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Parberry |first=Ian |date=25 March 1999 |title=1998 Gödel Prize. Seinosuke Toda |url=http://sigact.acm.org/Prizes/Godel/1998.html |url-status=deviated |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070517192431/http://sigact.acm.org/Prizes/Godel/1998.html |archive-date=17 May 2007 |website=ACM SIGACT}}</ref>

An analogous result in the complexity theory over the reals (in the sense of [[Blum–Shub–Smale machine|Blum–Shub–Smale real Turing machines]]) was proved by [[Saugata Basu]] and [[Thierry Zell]] in 2010<ref>{{cite journal |last=Basu |first=Saugata |last2=Zell |first2=Thierry |year=2010 |title=Polynomial Hierarchy, Betti Numbers and a Real Analogue of Toda's Theorem |url=http://www.math.purdue.edu/~sbasu/toda16.pdf |journal=Foundations of Computational Mathematics |volume=10 |pages=429–454 |doi=10.1007/s10208-010-9062-4}}</ref> and a complex analogue of Toda's theorem was proved by [[Saugata Basu]] in 2011.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Basu |first=Saugata |year=2011 |title=A Complex Analogue of Toda's Theorem |url=http://www.math.purdue.edu/~sbasu/focm_final-09-20-11.pdf |journal=Foundations of Computational Mathematics |volume=12 |pages=327–362 |doi=10.1007/s10208-011-9105-5}}</ref>

==Proof==
The proof is broken into two parts.

* First, it is established that
:: <math>\Sigma^P \cdot \mathsf{BP} \cdot \oplus \mathsf{P} \subseteq \mathsf{BP} \cdot \oplus \mathsf{P}</math>

:The proof uses a variation of [[Valiant–Vazirani theorem]]. Because <math>\mathsf{BP} \cdot \oplus \mathsf{P}</math> contains <math>\mathsf{P}</math> and is closed under complement, it follows by induction that <math>\mathsf{PH} \subseteq \mathsf{BP} \cdot \oplus \mathsf{P}</math>.

* Second, it is established that
:: <math>\mathsf{BP} \cdot \oplus \mathsf{P} \subseteq \mathsf{P}^{\# P}</math>

Together, the two parts imply
: <math>\mathsf{PH} \subseteq \mathsf{BP} \cdot \oplus \mathsf{P} \subseteq \mathsf{P} \cdot \oplus \mathsf{P} \subseteq \mathsf{P}^{\# P}</math>
See {{harvnb|Fortnow|2009}} for details.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Fortnow |first=Lance |date=3 July 2009 |title=A Simple Proof of Toda's Theorem |url=https://theoryofcomputing.org/articles/v005a007/|journal=Theory of Computing |volume=5 |pages=135–140 |doi=10.4086/toc.2009.v005a007 <!--typo in PDF copy-->|doi-access=free }}</ref> A more leisurely proof is in the textbook {{harvnb|Arora|Barak|2009}}.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Arora |first1=Sanjeev |title=Complexity Theory: A Modern Approach |last2=Barak |first2=Boaz |date=2009 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-0-511-80409-0 |chapter=17. Complexity of counting |chapter-url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/computational-complexity/complexity-of-counting/8C2E96892F02F64673C12931FCB900CC}}</ref>
